statement: Peter writes $1, 2, \ldots, 1001$ on 1001 cards arranged in a circle (face down). For each card $C$, $f(C)$ = number of the next 500 cards (clockwise) with a larger number. Prove Basil, seeing all $f(C)$ values, can determine the number on each card.

The tangent to circumcircle $\Omega$ of scalene $\triangle ABC$ at $C$ meets $AB$ at $D$. A line through $D$ meets $AC, BC$ at $K, L$. On $AB$: $M$ with $AC \parallel NL$ and $N$ with $BC \parallel KM$. $P = NL \cap KM$ (inside $\triangle ABC$); $\omega$ = circumcircle of $\triangle MNP$; $Q$ = second intersection of $CP$ with $\omega$. Show $DQ$ is tangent to $\omega$.

Natural numbers $a_1,\ldots,a_k$ are given; $S(n)$ = number of solutions to $a_1x_1+\cdots+a_kx_k = n$ in nonneg­ative integers; $S(n) > 0$ for all large $n$. Show $S(n+1) < 2S(n)$ for all sufficiently large $n$.
$n > 2$ nonzero reals sum to zero. Write all $2^n - 1$ nonempty subset sums in non-increasing order; the first is $S$. Find the smallest possible value of the second number.
Call $n$ \textit{good} if $n = ax^2 + bxy + cy^2$ for integers $a,b,c,x,y$ with $b^2 - 4ac = -20$. Prove the product of any two good numbers is also good.

Blue and green rectangles (horizontal/vertical sides) are placed on the plane. Any blue rectangle and any green rectangle can be separated by a vertical or horizontal line. Prove one can choose a color and three lines (two horizontal, one vertical) such that every rectangle of the chosen color is intersected by at least one of the lines.
